title: Anthony and the fish
hookLine: a legend: when no one listens, Anthony preaches to the fish

cards: A friar has walked into Rimini, a city on the sea, to preach, and nobody will listen. The Little Flowers says people there had turned against the Church's teaching, and they won't come to hear him.
The friar is Anthony, later known as Anthony of Padua, the finder of lost things this path met on his feast day. The obvious next move: leave. Shake the dust off.
Instead, Anthony walks down to where the river meets the sea, stands on the bank, and starts preaching to the water.

teach.h: HEAR THE WORD OF GOD, YOU FISHES.
teach.b: He calls out: hear the word of God, you fishes of the sea and of the river, since the people won't. And in the legend they come.

teach.h: HEADS ABOVE THE WATER, IN ORDER.
teach.b: So many fish gather that the water fills with them, all with their heads above the surface, all facing him, and in order: the little ones near the shore, the middle-sized behind them, the big ones out in the deep.
Then, like Francis with the birds, he counts out what God has given them.
Water, fresh and salt. Places to shelter from storms, and food.

When the flood came and the animals outside the ark perished, you were kept alive. God chose a fish to carry the prophet Jonah and set him safe on land. A fish brought up the coin that Peter paid as tax.
And after he rose, Christ himself ate fish. At this, the story says, the fish open their mouths and bow their heads, as if to praise. Word gets around.

People come running down to the river, and the ones who had refused to listen come too. They're moved, they fall at Anthony's feet, and now he preaches to them. That's the happy ending, but notice the order.
Anthony doesn't preach to the fish as a trick to win the crowd back. Nothing in the story says he expected anyone to come. He preached because preaching was his work, and the fish were who was there.
Paul tells Timothy, in the Douay-Rheims: "Preach the word: be instant in season, out of season." In season is when they're listening. Out of season is the riverbank.

how: Catholics honor Saint Anthony of Padua as a Franciscan preacher, and his sermon to the fish is a favorite subject in Franciscan art and storytelling.

games.q: what does “anthony and the fish” mean?
o: a miracle where Anthony fed a crowd with a few fish
a legend of Anthony preaching to fish when no one listened
a story of Anthony catching fish to feed poor friars

games.q: Anthony at Rimini — tap the pairs.

s: Anthony preached to the fish as a trick to draw a crowd
nothing in the story says he expected anyone. the people came after.
the fish gathered in order, small near the shore and big in the deep
the legend lines them up by size, heads above the water.
in the legend, the people of Rimini never came to listen
they came running to the river to see, fell at his feet, and he preached to them.

games.q: you're Anthony. you came to Rimini to preach, and nobody will listen. what do you do?
o: leave for a city that wants you.
go to the riverbank and preach to the fish.
stand in the square and scold them.
games.why: in the legend he preaches to the fish, and only afterward do the people come running to listen.

practice: Think of someone who doesn't really listen to you right now, a teenager behind a closed door, a coworker who talks past you, and instead of rehearsing the argument, find one true, kind sentence you could say to them.
Say it silently, slowly, as if to the water, and let go of whether it's heard. If you pray, give that sentence and that person to God.

wordCard.voice: Anthony and the fish. A legend of a preacher refused by a city, who preached to the fish, and was heard. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: preach anyway. The fish came first, and the crowd came later. Until tomorrow.
